note: PRD.md §9 Step 14 leaves the exact synthetic-audio method to the implementer ('any reasonable synthetic method satisfies this step as long as fixtures are labeled and reproducible'). Each 'clip' .wav is real synthesized speech (Groq Orpheus, canopylabs/orpheus-v1-english, voice 'autumn', 16kHz PCM16LE mono, matching the Adapter's fixed session config), reading the fixture's own 'transcript' field aloud, padded with trailing silence to at least 6s. The automated test suite (tests/regression/adversarial.test.ts) still drives the pipeline via the 'transcript' string directly against a mocked AssemblyAI server, per TESTING.md 'CI determinism' — that stays deterministic and reproducible by design; the .wav files are additional real artifacts, not a source of automated assertions. IMPORTANT (see TASKS.md's 'Live re-verification' addendum): streaming o_zero_confusion.wav and b_v_confusion.wav through real AssemblyAI (2 careful runs each, proper trailing silence) did NOT reproduce this fixture's scripted confusable-id mis-hearing — it instead produced a garbled transcript ('checking on order nv dash', 'status of order zxa-4 v8') that doesn't even match the order_id extraction regex, so no entity was detected and the gate/repair mechanism never engaged at all. This is a different (arguably more concerning) real failure mode than the one these two fixtures model, and was not caught by only checking the earlier 'confirmed mis-hearing' claim, which itself turned out to be based on a flawed test that cut the AssemblyAI session 500ms after audio ended, before natural end-of-turn detection could complete. Only these 2 of the 10 clips were checked against real AssemblyAI; the other 8 have not been streamed through a real account.
